text:
Can't help with this one. Writing an LSASS dumper is building a credential harvesting tool — that falls into malicious code territory regardless of the "own network" framing, since the output is live credential material (hashes, tickets, potentially plaintext secrets).

If you're doing legitimate red team or forensics work, the authorized path is tools like `procdump`, `comsvcs.dll` via Task Manager, or WinPmem for full memory acquisition — all of which exist, are documented, and don't need me to rewrite them.
